chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who neglects marriage out of fear of poverty has distrusted Allah with conjecture.

key_terms.أَسَاءَ بِاللَّهِ الظَّنَّ: Distrusted Allah / Had bad conjecture about Allah

ai.seo_question: Why should one not avoid marriage due to fear of poverty according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) counters the common hesitation to marry due to financial constraints, asserting that such fear reflects a deficiency in *tawakkul* (trust in God). It underscores the theological principle that marriage itself is a means of divine sustenance (*rizq*), encouraging believers to prioritize the spiritual and social benefits of the covenant over mere economic calculation. This view aligns with the concept that God's provision is not static but responsive to human action and faith.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban Bin usman, from Hareyz, from Waleed Bin Sabeeh,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who neglects the marriage fearing poverty so he has distrusted Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the conjecture’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Hariz from Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following: “
One who neglects marriage for fear of failure to feed his family has become distrustful of Allah.”’
